physical_claim_limit: Same 4d Hilbert-space Schmidt form has different operational nonlocality depending on tensor-factor locality and available reference/measurement resources. This is prior-art quantum foundations, not a novel Bell inequality or experimental result.

result.internal_two_DOF_state: one single photon with two internal qubit factors, |Phi+>=(|00>+|11>)/sqrt2
known_literature: Brask Chaves Brunner 2013, Phys Rev A 88 012111 single photon nonlocality reference frames, doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.88.012111
Hessmo et al 2004 Phys Rev Lett 92 180401 experimental single photon nonlocality doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.180401

result.loss_model: IID independent detection success probability eta per remote party, maximally entangled state, independent setting choices, zero single-party marginals, assign +1 to no clicks: S=2sqrt2 eta^2 + 2(1-eta)^2. This is NOT a general Bell-detection threshold.
result.physical_pitfalls: Physical spatial separation and independent settings, causal isolation, local coherent reference resources, heralding/postselection assumptions and detection efficiency are extra resources; Hilbert-space factorization inside one photon alone supplies none of these.
